, within the resistive MHD framework, ‘ideally’ tearing instability is a new mechanism for the initiation of fast magnetic reconnections in high- $S$ plasmas, and it is a natural extension of fast reconnection triggered via the plasmoid instability.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the absence of a magnetic guide field, the onset of fast reconnection is possible in the absence of resistivity.

, in the context of resistive MHD (or even more sophisticated kinetic plasma models), the onset of the ‘ideal’ instability is not only an efficient mechanism for fast reconnection but it also allows us to predict the time evolution of the reconnection rate in collapsing current sheets, and therefore to understand how fast reconnection can be triggered in high $S$ number plasmas.
